question: What does Talde et al. (2008) document about fish samples in the three named Agusan Marsh floodplain lakes, and can its lake-level labels be treated as a current inventory or independent dataset?

study.citation: Talde, C. M., Mamaril, A. C., Sr., & Palomares, M. L. D. (2008). Composition and length-weight relationships of fishes in the three floodplain lakes of Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary. Asian Fisheries Science, 21(1), 55-65. https://doi.org/10.33997/j.afs.2008.21.1.005.
study.fullTextAccess: Retrieved the linked PDF directly from the official Asian Fisheries Society publication page after the browser page parser failed to fetch the PDF. The downloaded PDF was reviewed locally from a temporary directory and was not added to the repository.
study.siteIdentityCaution: The paper calls these floodplain lakes of Agusan Marsh and locates them in northeast Mindanao. 'Dinagat' here is the lake name in Agusan Marsh, not evidence from Dinagat Islands province.

fieldPeriodDiscrepancy.methods: Monthly sampling from October 1998 to November 1999.
fieldPeriodDiscrepancy.table1: Catch-composition table caption says fish were caught between November 1998 and October 1999.
fieldPeriodDiscrepancy.interpretation: The one-month difference is unresolved; preserve both date ranges as source-specific rather than silently harmonizing them.

study.methodsSummary: The paper reports monthly fish samples from three traditional fishing floodplain lakes. It describes stationary gillnets and baited hook-and-line gears (palangri and kawil), including kawil deployed in shallow inundated lake-periphery areas. The described gear and habitat coverage are selective, not a complete faunal survey.
study.sampleSummary: Table 1 reports 764 fish across 14 taxon labels (12 binomial names and two genus-level labels). It includes a plus/minus lake-presence matrix, but the paper does not report a complete lake-by-taxon abundance table or exact capture coordinates. The abstract says length-weight parameters were estimated for nine species; that narrower analysis count is not the total taxon-label count in Table 1.
study.separateNarrativeReports: The discussion additionally mentions Mugil dussumieri from Lakes Dinagat and Mihaba and an unidentified local fish called 'ibis' from Lake Dinagat based on fisher reports during the study. These are described separately from the Table 1 catch matrix and are not added to its 764 count or converted into confirmed voucher-backed records.
study.dietBoundary: The article refers to the 2004 Talde et al. study for food-preference discussion; it is not an independent gut-content dataset and gives no new species-specific diet or bait recommendation in this review.
study.legalBoundary: Any mesh-size or electrofishing statements in this historical article are not current legal guidance; no current rule or regulation was verified.

crossStudyComparison.related2004Study: Talde et al. (2004) reports 578 gut samples and a similar monthly collection period in the same three named lakes. The two papers share authors and site/time context, so their samples may overlap, but no field-log crosswalk was found to prove the exact overlap or reconcile 578 gut samples with the 764-fish composition table.
crossStudyComparison.interpretation: Do not count the 2004 and 2008 papers as independent field surveys or add their sample counts. Retain their distinct study-specific methods and claims.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Publisher-hosted full text reviewed; historical catch table has lake-presence fields but no sample coordinates, vouchers, or per-lake count totals.
qualityAndRights.taxonomy: Names are preserved as printed. No new taxonomic, conservation-status, introduction-status, or specimen-identification review was performed for this article.
qualityAndRights.reuse: No article-level reuse license or permission statement was found in the reviewed PDF or article page. The article PDF is not stored in this repository; full table, image, and page contents are not reproduced here.
qualityAndRights.rightsDisposition: Research notes only; public-app use remains unapproved.

limits: This is a historical sampling period from 1998-1999, not a current occurrence survey, population estimate, or complete inventory.
The sampling-period end month differs between Methods and Table 1 captions.
Reported sample totals are pooled across three lakes; exact per-lake counts are not given in the reviewed table.
The table lists source-level names and lake-presence marks, not georeferenced specimens or voucher identifiers.
The two genus-level labels remain unresolved and must not be expanded to species names.
The additional fisher-reported Mugil dussumieri and unidentified 'ibis' observations are kept separate from table sampling.
Potential overlap with the authors' 2004 Agusan Marsh gut-content study is not resolved; do not treat the papers as independent samples.
No diet, bait, current safety, legal rule, water-quality, geometry, or current catchability claim is inferred.

references.supports: Official publication metadata, abstract, authorship, issue, page range, and link to the publisher PDF.
Full publisher PDF reviewed locally, including Methods, Table 1 and discussion; no copy added to repository.
Third-party-hosted full text used for the related 2004 study review; not an independent publisher record or permission for reuse.

nextAction: Continue Caraga freshwater coverage with a primary source from another named inland waterbody or a current, independently voucher-linked survey. For these three Agusan Marsh lakes, seek an authorized dataset or collection record that resolves taxon-to-lake and sample-to-voucher links; keep the 1998-1999 matrix research-only.
